sub_palette: celtic (goidelic) backbone + near_eastern (old_persian / axsatran) overlay (cross-family blend, Celtic-leaning)

blend.backbone: celtic (Insular / Goidelic register: ri/ruiri/ard-ri, tuath, dun/rath forts, Mac-/O- patronymics, initial consonant mutation, broad-slender consonants, root-initial stress - the horse-clans of the saddle and the cattle-raid)
blend.overlay: near_eastern (old_persian / axsatran: the -pura cities and dida-citadels, the satrapal Xshacapavan/Marzapana office-register, the paridaida garden-courts, the poet-king populace, vowel-rich Indo-Iranian phonology flowing into poetic meter, the genitive '-ahya')
blend.lean: Celtic-heavy - a Goidelic horse-clan warrior-aristocracy (steppe-touched riders, Scythian-contacted Celts, a ri-house of the saddle) ridden down onto the Iranian plateau and enthroned over the refined Persian heartland: the cattle-and-horse clans rule by the spear and the boast, the courtly poet-king cities and their satrapal scribes endure and serve beneath. Horse-clans of the West over the land of poet-kings.

_note: NEW cross-family hybrid under the base/hybrid model. BASE_02 (Celtic; the Goidelic horse-clans) x BASE_04 (Persian; the axsatran heartland). CIV/CLAN DECIDED by inheritance: Celtic base = Clanhold, Persian base = Civilized, and any Civ parent -> Civ, so Zaralba is Civilized (feudal). Concept: the Celts had real steppe/Scythian contact; here a Goidelic horse-clan aristocracy has ridden the steppe down onto the Iranian plateau and set itself up as kings over the refined Persian courtly heartland (the land of poet-kings). Backbone = Celtic (Goidelic/Insular: the ruling clan-warrior-aristocracy of riders, the ri/ruiri/ard-ri register, Mac-/O- patronymics, the PRIMARY deity reflexes from family_celtic's theonym_set); overlay/substrate = Persian (the existing -pura cities, the dida-citadels, the satrapal Xshacapavan office, the courtly-poetic populace, the SECONDARY deity-morphs from axsatran). Common-word lexicon and rank titles use the real Gaelic and Old-Persian registers (allowed, catalog 5.3); DEITY names are morphs of the Agrippan canon from both parents (Celtic Goidelic reflexes primary, Old-Persian/axsatran variants secondary), never real Celtic/Iranian/Zoroastrian gods (no Lugh/Dagda/Morrigan, no Ahura Mazda/Mithra). The kingdom-tier DISPLAY ruler is the approved foreign term 'Shah' (the Persian substrate's iconic throne-title, recorded in approved_foreign_terms_used); all other display tiers are English, conlang forms in ruler_native/domain_native for NPC dialogue. The cardinal Persian virtue ARTA (Truth/Right-order) and its opposite DRAUGA (the Lie) carry over as the court's moral vocabulary, fused with the Celtic warrior-oath and the geis (the binding vow). The realm is broadly TOLERANT in the Persian manner - the ruiri shelters the subject cults beneath the crown. [UPDATE 2026-06-27: all human cultures allow Lawful/Neutral/Chaotic; ruler/domain DISPLAY titles are English (or an approved foreign term); conlang titles live in ruler_native/domain_native. Deities via the per-family morph method.]

phonology.palette: Insular Celtic (Goidelic) backbone - initial consonant mutation (lenition c>ch, b>bh/v, m>mh/v, t>th, d>dh; nasalization), broad vs slender consonants, vowels a e i o u (long marks dropped in data), root-initial stress, the Mac-/O- patronymics - meeting an Old Persian overlay: vowels a i u with long a/i/u, the spirants th/x(kh)/f, sibilants s/sh/z and c(ts), the clusters xsh-/sp-/st-/fr-/thr-, the characteristic endings -a/-ah/-iya/-ana/-aspa(horse)/-arta(truth)/-farnah(glory). Per the CSV: lyrical Celtic vowels flowing into a poetic Persian court-meter; grammar shifts toward SOV with the Persian Ezafe linker carried under Celtic initial mutations (SOV, Ezafe with initial mutations). Theophoric on the Goidelic reflexes (Toran-, Orlann-) with Old-Persian construct variants (Turvasa-, Urlaspa-, Arta-).
phonology.phonotactics: CV/CVC meeting CV(C); Goidelic mutation-driven clusters and broad-slender contrast alongside Old Persian xsh-/sp-/fr-/thr-; root-initial Celtic stress softened by a Persian heavy-syllable and poetic court-meter; vowel length distinctive (the Persian flowing vowels); Goidelic Dun-/Rath- forts over Dida-/-pura/-stana toponyms; the Persian Ezafe and genitive-of-relation '-ahya' under Celtic lenition.

sound_changes: Persian flowing/long vowels and bare vowel-endings adapted to Goidelic shape: final -a/-ah/-ana/-aya>0 or to a Goidelic -an/-ach; long a/i/u shortened; vowel-final roots take a Goidelic consonant-coda where a stem would otherwise float

Persian exotic phonemes collapse into the Goidelic inventory: xsh->c(broad)/ch, z->s, v->bh/v, syllabic -spa/-zraka cluster-onsets simplified to Goidelic stops; the th/x spirants reread as Goidelic lenited th/ch

Goidelic lenition and broad/slender harmony imposed on every inherited root (c>ch, b>bh/v, m>mh/v, d>dh; a broad root takes a broad ending, a slender root a slender one), so Persian substrate words mutate exactly like native ones
Goidelic root-initial stress on all words; the Persian penultimate/heavy-syllable pull dropped; Persian construct-chains and Ezafe collapse to a single stressed compound

retain Goidelic ch, bh/mh, broad-slender contrast and the dun-/rath- shape; retain an audible Persian flavour in the surviving spirant-rich vowel-runs (the -ah/-ar/-an cadence) and the -arta/-farnah signature stems
fusion_rules.source_tilt: land/terrain/material/staple words from Old-Persian (axsatran) roots (the courtly plateau-substrate that works and names the land: rautah>rath-vowel, kaufa, vana, ayah, yava, aspa, zaranya); kin-line/quality/abstract/rule/war words from Goidelic roots (the ruling horse-clan register: mac, mor, sean, ard, fior, ri, sluag); every chosen root then run through the one Goidelic sound-law so the split is inaudible

lexicon._note: Single fused tongue derived via phonology.fusion_rules (gdd-hybrid-conlang-fusion.md): Old-Persian (axsatran) land/material/staple roots + Goidelic kin/rule/quality/war roots, all run through one Goidelic-shaped sound-law (lenition, broad-slender, root-initial stress); portmanteaus mark the blended bloodline and the shared institutions. Celtic-lean: it sounds Goidelic even where the root rode in from the plateau.

morphology.patronymic_form: the Goidelic ruling clan keeps the Mac- (son of) and O-/Ua- (descendant of) patronymic and the fine/cland kin-group; the Persian populace keep the filiation 'X-ahya puthra' (son of X) or compact 'X-puthra' and a house (vith-X) or office; the throne fuses both - a ri who also bears a vith- house-name and a satrapal seat.
morphology.compounding_rule: Goidelic compound ([quality|feature|saint](stem) + element: Dun-derg, red-fort; Ard-mor, great-height) layered over Old Persian relation-compounds and construct via '-ahya' and the Ezafe (Arta-xshaca, truth-realm; Dida-[name], fort of; [name]-pura, city of): the capital Dunfarnah (the glory-fort), Dida-Conn (citadel of the Conn-house).

title_ladder.government: feudal (a Goidelic horse-clan aristocracy over the Persian satrapal heartland: the ruiri (over-king) and his flaith-kin in the saddle at the crown, the tigerna-lords and the Persian Xshacapavan-satraps over the -pura cities, the marcaigh-riders and the king's-warriors sworn to the war-host; the magi tend the fire and the scribal court endures beneath; the brithem-judge and the fili-poet stand outside the ladder)
title_ladder._tiers_note: Goidelic clanhold ladder, ascending, with the Old-Persian satrapal substrate co-titles beneath. Toisech (clan-chief / leader) barony over a Toisecheacht; Flaith-criche (border-lord) march over a Crich (the border-march); Tigerna (lord) county; Flaith (noble-lord) duchy ruling over a Xshacapavanam (the Persian SATRAPY he holds as a war-fief); Ri-tuaithe (king of a tuath) principality over a Tuath (petty kingdom); Ruiri (over-king) kingdom over a Mor-tuath (great tuath) - the kingdom DISPLAY title is the approved foreign 'Shah' from the Persian substrate; Ard-ri (high king) empire over the Vispa-tuath (the 'all-the-tuatha', Gmc Persian Vispa- + Goid. tuath). The subject cities keep their Persian Xshacapavan (satrap) and Framatar (appointed governor) and Marzapana (march-warden) beneath the Goidelic crown. The brithem (judge), the fili/ollam (poet-sage), the gudja-druid and the Persian magu stand outside the ladder. Rank titles fuse the real Gaelic and Old-Persian registers (allowed).
title_ladder.heir: Tanaiste (the second; the designated heir) / Mathishta (the greatest; crown prince)
title_ladder.display_policy: Ruler/domain titles shown in setting-gen, domain lists and vassal trees are ENGLISH (or an approved commonly-known foreign term where set in 'ruler'). The *_native conlang forms are for NPC DIALOGUE ONLY, never for structural/UI displays.

people_name_convention.order: the Goidelic ruling stock carry a given name + Mac-/O- patronymic or fine/cland; the Persian populace carry a theophoric or Arta-/Vahu- virtue given name + filiation (X-puthra); order given-first.
people_name_convention.dual_register: the Goidelic war-aristocracy keep Gaelic names (Conn-, Niall-, Bran-, Mac-/O- patronymics, the deed/animal byname); the Persian court-and-city folk keep theophoric and virtue names (Turvasa-data, Arta-X, Vahu-X) on the morphed canon-stems with the -puthra filiation.
people_name_convention.theophoric: Celtic devotional on the Goidelic god-reflexes (Mael-Toran, the devotee of Toran; Gilla-Orlann, the servant of Orlann); Persian devotional constructs on the shifted stems and on Arta- (Truth): Turvasa-data (Turvasa-given), Baga-Urlaspa, Artafarnah, Vahu-Arzanta.

religion._note: Deity-names are morphs of the Agrippan canon - Celtic Goidelic reflexes PRIMARY (family_celtic theonym_set: Toran, Orlann, Gaian, Numan, Realtan, Eternan, Dolar, Nochtluan, Raithan), Old-Persian/axsatran variants SECONDARY (the axsatran shifted morphs: Turvasa, Urlaspa, Gayanta, Naumana, Riyata, Asturna), never real Celtic/Iranian/Zoroastrian gods. The cardinal Persian virtue ARTA (Truth/Right-order) and its opposite DRAUGA (the Lie) carry over as the court's moral vocabulary, fused with the Celtic warrior-oath and the geis (the binding vow); the breaking of a geis is the Celtic face of the Lie. Alignment per the standard lens (Lawful/Neutral/Chaotic): the Celtic warrior-oath and the Persian Arta tradition read Lawful-friendly, the horse-clans' ancestor-cult and the cattle-raid reads Neutral, the wild Chaotic powers of the hunt and the war-fire keep their cults. The realm is broadly TOLERANT in the Persian manner - the ruiri shelters the subject cults beneath the crown.
religion.the_one: Eternan (Celtic; Persian Asturna) - the distant Ancient One and Wise Lord Most High, upholder of Arta, honored not petitioned

sample_deity_renames.Tulrius: Toran (Pers. Turvasa) - the sun, fire, light, and justice; the lamp of right-order
sample_deity_renames.Orlandus: Orlann (Pers. Urlaspa) - iron, oath, war, and the cavalier
sample_deity_renames.Gaiandus: Gaian (Pers. Gayanta) - the enduring earth, cold, and mountain
sample_deity_renames.Numeno: Numan (Pers. Naumana) - air, lightning, sky-wisdom, and the good-mind
sample_deity_renames.Realta: Realtan (Pers. Riyata) - the mother, mercy, healing, the Lady of Waters

worship_by_alignment.Lawful: venerates the Lawful powers - Eternan, Toran the just, Orlann of the sworn war, Realtan the merciful - upholding Arta (right-order) and naming the Chaotic powers the hosts of Drauga the Lie, warded as the fomoraig (the demon-brood); the warrior-oath, the geis, and the king's-word-as-bond bind alike
worship_by_alignment.Neutral: the ancestral war-dead (the deified champions of the ruling clan) honored as the sinnsir (the forefathers) and as fravashi (fore-spirits), and the land-spirits of the nemed-grove and the -pura; the great powers and Nochtluan of the moon invoked at the nemed and the fire-altar situationally; the cattle-raid and the saddle stand under no single power
worship_by_alignment.Chaotic: Venerates the Chaotic powers of the canon - Raithan of the red hunt, Maragan the war-brand - and names the Lawful powers, and Eternan, as the tyrant-gods to be defied.

religion.demon_epithet_pattern: the Chaotic powers, warded as the fomoraig (Celtic demon-brood) or the hosts of Drauga (the Persian Lie), keep their morphs + an epithet: Maraxus -> Maragan the War-Brand (Pers. Marakhsha the Burner-of-Cities); Vacidus -> Faicid the Unmaker (Pers. Vakida the Devouring-Void); Lusanto -> Losand the Hoard-Worm (Pers. Lusanta the Coin-Serpent).

clergy_ladder.5: Sacart-mor (consecrated priest) / Magupati (chief magus of a fire-temple)
clergy_ladder.9: Sinnsear-drui (eldest druid) / Magupatan Magupat (chief of chief magi)

religion.religious_orders_pattern: the Nemed (Celtic sacred grove) or the Atashana (Persian fire-temple) of [power]: 'the Nemed of Toran', 'the Atashana of Turvasa'; the druids keep the grove and the magi keep the ever-burning fire (Atar) on the altar.
religion.saints_pattern: the sinnsir (the deified champions and forefathers of the ruling clan) and the honest dead and just kings of the Persian cities, kept as fravashi (fore-spirits) and honored at the cairn, the standing stone, and the fire-altar; 'the Fior-true [name]' (the righteous [name]).

holy_symbol_motifs.Toran: a rayed sun-wheel over a crossed sword and the upright Arta-measure
holy_symbol_motifs.Orlann: an iron spear crossed with an oath-ring (the geis-ring)
holy_symbol_motifs.Gaian: the enduring mountain beneath the winged ring-disc (the farnah-glory)

banks_patterns.ships: the few river-barges and royal-road craft of a horse-and-cattle power: 'Pride of the Abann', 'Bearer of the Baji', 'Boat of Turvasa'
banks_patterns.military_units: the ruiri's sluag (war-host) and the Persian-style cavalry guard: 'the Sluag of Zaralba', 'the Spada of Urlaspa', 'the Iron Marcaigh (the riders of the plateau)'
banks_patterns.taverns: 'The [Adjective] [Noun]': 'The Golden Farnah', 'The Hound and Cup', 'The Cup of Truth (Arta-jam)'
banks_patterns.dungeons_ruins: fallen apadana-halls, dead fire-temples, and sunken Celtic raths: 'the buried Apadana of Dida-[name]', 'the dead Atashana of [name]', 'the Cairn of the Conn-clan'

clan_houses: the Ui Chuinn (ruling house - the Conn-clan)
